catalog_quote: 1. do³ ~ ɗo³ 2. sɔ² 3. ta³ 4. ⁱhɪɛ̃⁴ 5. ŋʷũ⁴² 6. ŋʷũ⁴² kloː²⁴ (5+1) ... 10. ŋʷũ⁴² bu⁴ or bu⁴ 11. bue⁴⁴ do³ ... 20. ɡᵓlɔ³ ... Other comments: Wané has a quinary, vigesimal system similar to that of Bakwé. Tone marks used above areː v²=high; v⁴²=sharp rise low tone, v²⁴=drop in the last tone. Wané or Hwane, Ngwané is spoken by approximately 2,100 speakers in Bas-Sassandra district: Kounoukou area on southwest coast, Côte d'Ivoire.

new_statements.rule_in_words: First-hand SIL transcription of Wané numerals with lexical tone numbers on every syllable (level 2 = high, levels 3 and 4 lower; contour 42 'sharp rise low tone', 24, 44), i.e. Wané is treated as a register-tone language with at least three levels plus contours; nothing is said about stress or accent. This is a tone-marked numeral list with a legend, not a phonological description — marginal as a 'statement'.
new_statements.identity_note: Page header 'Wané, Bas-Sassandr[a], Côte d'Ivoire [Refer to Ethnologue]'; comments: 'Wané or Hwane, Ngwané is spoken by approximately 2,100 speakers in Bas-Sassandra district: Kounoukou area on southwest coast' = Ethnologue hwa; data from the SIL Bakwé-project linguist; numerals match Delafosse 1904 Houané (lo/ɗo, sò, ta, hyĩ, hũ) and are distinct from Leidenfrost's Bakwé page.

sources.citation: Delafosse, Maurice. 1904. Vocabulaires comparatifs de plus de 60 langues ou dialectes parlés à la Côte d'Ivoire et dans les régions limitrophes. Paris: Ernest Leroux. [Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description for wane1242, 'a wordlist or less']
sources.note: Wané ('Hwine ou Hwané (Houané), appelés aussi Bodo', p. 70) is represented only by a 1-10 numeral column in the 'Groupe bakoué' table (p. 74), collected by G. Thomann. The general introduction (p. 3) says only that 'l'accent tonique ou plutôt l'intonation' cannot be marked alphabetically; no Wané-specific accent note.

sources.citation: Thomann, Georges. 1905. Essai de manuel de la langue néouolé parlée dans la partie occidentale de la Côte d'Ivoire; ouvrage accompagné d'un recueil de contes et chansons en langue néouolé, d'une étude sur les diverses tribus bêté-bakoué, de vocabulaires comparatifs, d'une bibliographie et d'une carte. Paris: Ernest Leroux. Septième partie, II 'Le néouolé comparé aux autres dialectes de la famille bêté-bakoué', pp. 189-193: numeral table 'Groupe bakoué' with a column 'dialecte de Victory' [= Bodo / Houané = Wané] and fold-out comparative vocabulary.
sources.note: nothing; bare comparative wordlist. Value: earliest attributable Wané (Bodo/Victory) data and the source behind Delafosse 1904's Houané numerals; adds a second pre-SIL Wané wordlist to the bibliography.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid pages wane1242, bakw1242 (Bakwe-Wane), bakw1243 (Bakwé), east2415, and reference records 589953 / 60421 / 308018; Glottolog langdoc search for 'wané', 'bakwé', 'hwane'.
sources.note: Wané, Bakwé and the Bakwe-Wane group all carry the same three comparative references (Vogler 2017, Marchese 1989, Zogbo 2012) plus Ethnologue; Glottolog's most extensive description for Wané is Delafosse 1904 (a wordlist or less). No descriptive reference exists; langdoc searches return nothing.
